title: ER Modeling
description: Entities, attributes, relationships, and turning diagrams into tables.

questions.prompt: A student has many courses — a one-to-many. What does this print?
questions.explanation: Two courses on the 'many' side — length is 2.

questions.prompt: A student takes many courses and a course has many students. What's wrong?
options: Cardinality should be many-to-many, not one-to-one
questions.explanation: Both sides can have many — the diagram must show many-to-many.
Nouns first, then the diagram, then relationships, then tables.

questions.prompt: In ER diagrams, relationships are drawn as ___.
questions.explanation: Rectangles = entities, ovals = attributes, diamonds = relationships.

questions.prompt: Match each ER shape to its meaning.

pairs.definition: A thing worth tracking, drawn as a rectangle
A property of an entity, drawn as an oval
A connection between entities, drawn as a diamond

questions.prompt: This entity — which SQL creates it as a table?
questions.explanation: Entity → table, attributes → columns, key attribute → primary key.
Index 0 of the students array — the first on the 'many' side.

questions.prompt: OrderItem is meant to be a weak entity of Order. What's wrong?
options: A weak entity needs its parent's key — item_name alone can't identify it
questions.explanation: Weak entities borrow identity: the key should include order_id.

questions.prompt: A many-to-many relationship becomes a ___ table holding both keys.
questions.explanation: The junction table holds one row per pair, with both foreign keys.

questions.prompt: Which JavaScript models the same entity?
questions.explanation: A table is an array of row-objects; columns become properties.
